findings.evidence: Err(error) => return Err(format!("rates feed {url}: {error} after {ATTEMPTS} attempts")),
findings.recommendation: When the feed fails on its last attempt or returns a body that does not parse, the function returns an `Err` string without emitting any event: only the intermediate retries produce a `warn!`, and an invalid body produces nothing at all. Since the proposal says the caller silently keeps the previous day's rates, an outage of the central bank feed (or a format change) can leave stale rates in use for days with no error-level event an operator could alert on. Emit an `error!` with fields (attempts, error, stage such as "http" or "decode") before returning the error, so stale rates are visible. Confidence is low because no caller exists yet in the diff: a caller that logs the error at error level would cover it.
findings.title: Final fetch failure leaves no log or signal of its own
